newsitem.title: CANADA: Spanish trawler banned from area off Canada.
newsitem.headline: Spanish trawler banned from area off Canada.

text.p: A Spanish trawler has been banned from fishing in an area off Canada's east coast, the government of Canada said on Monday.

Canadian Fisheries Minister Fred Mifflin said European Union (EU) inspectors promptly boarded the Spanish vessel Hermanos Gandon IV in response to a report by Canadian inspectors that the boat had misreported its catch.

These arrangements had been put into place after Spain and Canada nearly came to blows in March 1995 when Canada declared a ban on fishing in a rich area just outside its 200-mile (320 km) limit to protect the endangered turbot, or Greenland halibut.
"The minister praised European Union ... inspectors for their prompt and effective enforcement action," a statement from Mifflin's office said.

Canadian inspectors boarded the vessel on Feb. 27 and contacted an EU patrol vessel, which boarded it on March 1. EU inspectors confirmed it had about 33.8 tonnes of turbot where the master had reported only 14.8 tonnes in his log.

The statement said Spanish authorities revoked the vessel's license to fish in the area for the rest of the year and told Canada the boat would be subject to a substantial fine, a sign that the bitter transatlantic fishing dispute of two years ago was past.
